notes.meaning: A farmer controls where water flows by digging small ditches through his fields. In the same way, the Lord has full control over the minds and choices of kings. Even the most powerful rulers on earth are guided by God to carry out His purposes.

People easily convince themselves that whatever they do is right and fair. God, however, looks straight past outward excuses and weighs our real motives. His judgment is always accurate because He examines the hidden thoughts of the heart.

Living an honest life and treating others fairly pleases God far more than religious ceremonies. Performing outward rituals can never make up for treating people unjustly. True worship begins with a heart that loves mercy and acts right.

Looking down on others comes from a heart swollen with pride. When people live only for themselves and ignore God, everything they cultivate and pursue becomes tainted by sin. Even their everyday work turns evil because they shut God out of their lives.

Steady hard work and careful planning bring plenty of food and supplies. On the other hand, rushing carelessly to get rich without proper thought leads straight to poverty. True success requires patience and good judgment, not reckless shortcuts.

Money gathered through dishonesty and lying disappears as quickly as morning mist. It offers no lasting peace and leaves a person empty inside. Those who build their fortune on deceit are really heading straight into the trap of death.

The cruelty and robbery carried out by evil people will sweep them away like a flood. Their own crimes end up becoming their ruin. Because they stubbornly refuse to do what is fair, their punishment catches up with them.

A person loaded down with guilt walks along twisted and sneaky paths to hide his faults. An innocent person has nothing to hide and walks in a straight, honest way. Pure motives produce clean, upright conduct.

Living in a cramped, exposed corner of a flat roof is better than sharing a roomy house with an argumentative wife. Constant quarreling ruins the comfort of a home. Peace in a small, rough shelter is worth far more than luxury filled with strife.

Wicked people have an appetite for doing harm and causing trouble. They have no sympathy even for their closest neighbors or friends. Anyone who gets in their way will be treated harshly and shown no mercy.

When an arrogant scorner is openly punished, inexperienced people take warning and gain wisdom. At the same time, wise people do not need painful discipline to learn. They simply listen to good teaching and quickly take it to heart.

God, the righteous Judge, keeps His eye on the household of the wicked. Though evildoers may seem prosperous for a season, He sees the curse hanging over them. At the right time, He brings their whole structure down in ruin.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Following the Latin Vulgate, this verse is traditionally read as a righteous person watching over the house of the wicked in order to turn them away from evil.

notes.meaning: Anyone who ignores the pleas of poor and hurting people will one day face trouble of their own. When that selfish person cries out for help, neither God nor neighbor will answer. Those who show no mercy will receive no mercy.

A quiet present given in private has great power to calm down furious anger. It can turn away deep resentment before it boils over. While gifts can smooth over personal quarrels, sneaking bribes to corrupt justice is still shameful.

Upright people feel genuine happiness whenever justice is carried out. On the other hand, fair laws and just punishments terrify wrongdoers. Living by the truth brings joy to the good, but it exposes and threatens those who practice evil.

A person who wanders off the path of wisdom and sound judgment ends up lost. That wandering leads straight to the graveyard of the ungodly. Unless such a traveler turns back, his final resting place will be among the ruined dead.

People who chase constant entertainment, expensive wine, and luxury oils will soon lose their money. Wasteful feasting drains away family savings. A life given over to selfish pleasures leads straight to poverty.

In God's providence, the trouble planned for the righteous often turns around and falls on the wicked instead. The upright are set free, while the troublemaker takes their place in judgment. Evildoers end up trapped in the very net they laid for others.

It is better to endure the heat and loneliness of an empty desert than to live with an ill-tempered, nagging wife. Harsh words and constant anger make close relationships miserable. Quiet solitude is far more peaceful than endless arguing.

Wise people manage their resources with care, storing up food and useful goods for their families. A foolish person, however, immediately swallows down whatever comes into his hands. Sensible thrift preserves wealth, while reckless spending destroys it.

Anyone who eagerly pursues fair living and loving-kindness receives abundant blessings. God gives such a person true spiritual life, an upright character, and lasting honor. Caring for others is the surest way to find real satisfaction.

A wise man can capture a fortress guarded by powerful soldiers because wisdom is stronger than brute force. Skillful planning outmatches mere muscle and weapons. The high walls that proud fighters trust in cannot stand against sound judgment.
Learning to watch what you say keeps your life out of painful traps. Rash and hurtful words cause arguments, guilt, and deep sorrow. A guarded tongue protects the heart from endless trouble.

A person who is swollen with pride and looks down on everyone else earns the name of mocker. Such an arrogant man acts with uncontrollable fury whenever he is challenged. His pride makes him quick to insult others and slow to show respect.

Lazy people sit around wishing for food and comforts, but their hands refuse to do any real work. Their unsatisfied longings torment them and eventually lead to starvation and ruin. In contrast, honest, hard-working people gain plenty for themselves and have enough left over to give generously to others.

Religious gifts brought by wicked people are detestable to God because their hearts remain corrupt. It is even worse when they bring an offering to cover up a dishonest scheme or buy permission to keep on sinning. God will not let religious rituals be used as a mask for evil deeds.

A witness who lies in court will eventually be caught and ruined. In contrast, a person who listens carefully and testifies only to what is true will be heard and believed. Lies collapse over time, but the truth stands firm to the end.

A wicked man puts on a bold, shameless face and stubbornly pushes forward in his sin. An upright person does not act rashly, but stops to examine his path carefully. He guides his daily steps by God's commands rather than stubborn pride.

No human wisdom, clever strategy, or advice can ever win against the Lord. Armies must still train their horses and ready their weapons for battle, but weapons alone cannot save anyone. True safety and victory belong entirely to God.
